rachel: Hi all 1st day and hit a weird one. VPN (Okta AnyConnect split-tunnel) works on Windows but inside WSL2 my hostnames like `api.internal.redwood.dev` resolve to public IPs or time out. Windows `nslookup api.internal.redwood.dev` returns 10.40.5.8, WSL `dig api.internal.redwood.dev` returns a public IP. Anyone seen DNS not following the VPN into WSL?
tom: yup, seen this. WSL2 often uses its own DNS settings and `/etc/resolv.conf` can get regenerated. After VPN connects Windows' DNS is correct but the WSL VM still has the old resolver.
rachel: is there a safe fix? i tried editing `/etc/resolv.conf` but it gets overwritten on restart.
devex: two options: (A) prevent WSL from auto-generating resolv.conf and write a small script to copy Windows DNS when VPN connects, (B) use the bastion/proxy for tools that need internal names. If you want persistent DNS inside WSL do this:

1) in WSL: `sudo rm /etc/resolv.conf` and then `echo "generateResolvConf = false" | sudo tee /etc/wsl.conf`
2) restart WSL: from PowerShell run `wsl --shutdown` and then open WSL again after VPN is up
3) create `/etc/resolv.conf` manually with the Windows VPN DNS server (e.g., `nameserver 10.40.1.2`) so WSL will use the internal resolver

That stops WSL from regenerating it. Note: you need to update the file if the VPN DNS changes.
tom: small alternative that avoids sudo: run a helper from PowerShell after the VPN connects to copy the current Windows DNS into WSL: `wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf <<'EOF'
nameserver $(powershell -command "(Get-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceAlias 'vEthernet (WSL)')")
EOF"` (we have a snippet in onboarding docs).
infra-bot: Docs: https://wiki.redwood.internal/vpn/wsl-dns-note and ticket template if infra should push a policy for managed laptops.
rachel: thanks all 1 did the generateResolvConf=false route and updated `/etc/resolv.conf` to the VPN DNS, now `dig` returns internal IPs and docker-compose can reach internal services. i'll add this to my onboarding notes and ping infra if it becomes a repeated pain.
